rationale: The buyer is specific and named — a freelance or independent software contractor on a paid engagement, with real professional and financial stakes (contract liability, legal exposure) — and this type of professional demonstrably pays for tools that protect their business (E&O insurance, code-review tooling, legal templates). Willingness to pay is supported by adjacent paid markets: Codacy and SonarQube are paid products; legal document templates for contractors command $50–200 one-time fees. The service — generate a timestamped, auditable AI-code-review scope report with a coverage disclaimer the contractor can attach to delivery emails — is entirely buildable as a Claude prompt pipeline with a simple web intake and PDF output, and once built it runs hands-off: the contractor submits a code diff or repo link, Claude produces the report, Stripe collects $15–30 per report or a $49/month subscription. The deciding factor is that the buyer has money, a clear reason to pay now (active liability exposure), and the product requires zero per-customer human work.
solution_plan: WHAT: An AI-code-review liability shield — a web service that takes a repo diff or pasted code and generates a professional audit-scope report with timestamped coverage disclaimers a contractor can attach to client deliveries. BUILD: Claude prompt pipeline that analyzes submitted code, identifies AI-generated patterns, and outputs a structured PDF report (scope covered, limitations, disclaimer language); a one-page landing page with a Stripe payment link ($25/report or $49/month); an email/web intake form — all assembled by the factory, no operator coding. SELL: Reach freelance contractors via Toptal community forums, r/freelance, Indie Hackers, and LinkedIn posts targeting 'freelance software contractor' — Claude drafts outreach targeting people discussing AI code liability; operator approves each send batch. MAINTAIN: Report delivery is fully automated (Claude generates, PDF renderer outputs, email sends via automation); Stripe handles billing and receipts; support FAQs handled by Claude. Operator's only recurring task: approve outreach batches and review weekly revenue dashboard. A solo non-technical operator can build and run this entirely through the factory.
notes: All build_gates met: operational_autonomy=8 (≥7), buildability_with_ai=8 (≥6), buyer_clarity=8 (≥6), willingness_to_pay=6 (≥5). Responsiveness_signal is 1 — untested; recommend a small outreach probe before full build commit.
